newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian OLOs rebound on post-auction demand.
newsitem.headline: Belgian OLOs rebound on post-auction demand.

text.p: Belgian linear bonds rebounded from early lows in late trading on Monday, aided by investor demand for the government's new bond issue and a stable U.S. Treasury market, dealers said.

With the Belgian Treasury allocating only a small percentage -- 13 percent -- of the 2006 OLO at the stop-out rate, traders said post-auction demand from investors unable to obtain the securities contributed to the market's better performance.
"They were limited at the stop price and so you try to buy back in the market," said one trader.
The Belgian 2006 OLO was sold at an average yield of 6.65 percent.
Another contributing factor was a stable opening in the U.S. bond market, dealers said. Belgian bonds were sharply lower in early trading following a selloff in U.S. bonds on Friday.
The OLO/Bund spread also widened back to 27 in afternoon dealings after narrowing to 22 this morning.
Overall, dealers said activity was light with the London market closed for a summer holiday.
"The market does not have high turnover with the U.K. closed," said another trader.
